author: continuation_consolidation
note: bars[0] is the reference (most recently closed) bar; index increases going back in time. For the three-methods and mat-hold predicates the long anchor bar is bars[4] (oldest); those five bars are all supplied explicitly so no filler lands inside the read span. Bars are [open, high, low, close, tick_volume].

fixtures.rationale: Rising three methods is a bullish continuation: a long white bar (bar4: 100->109), then three small bearish pullback bars (bars 3,2,1) that stay inside the long bar's 99..110 range, then a strong white bar (bar0) that closes at 111.5, above the long bar's 110 high. Every clause holds.

The final bar is bullish but closes at 108.5, still below the long bar's 110 high, so the continuation never breaks out. Without the breakout it is just a pullback that failed to resume, not rising three methods.

Bar2 dips to a low of 98, below the long bar's 99 low, so the pullback is no longer contained within the long bar. A pullback that pierces the long bar's low is a breakdown, not a healthy continuation setup.
Bar1 closes at 105.5 above its 103 open, making it bullish. The three middle bars must be a bearish pullback; a bullish middle bar breaks the down-drift the pattern requires.
close[0]=111 is above the long bar's high[4]=110, so the strict close>high breakout clause fires true. Kept clearly above 110 to avoid float-equality ambiguity.
Identical to the breakout-inside case except close[0]=109 is below high[4]=110, so the close>high breakout clause is false. The final bar is still bullish, isolating the breakout clause.
Bar1 high=109.9 is within the long bar's high[4]=110, so high[1]<=high[4] holds and the containment clause passes. Everything else stays at the positive canonical values.
Only change from the containment-inside case: bar1 high=110.1 is beyond high[4]=110, so high[1]<=high[4] fails. Single isolated change identifies the containment clause as the rejecter.

Falling three methods is the bearish mirror: a long black bar (bar4: 110->101), three small bullish bars (bars 3,2,1) that stay inside the 100..111 range, then a strong black bar (bar0) closing at 99, below the long bar's 100 low. All clauses hold.
The final bar is bearish but closes at 101, still above the long bar's 100 low, so no downside breakdown occurs. The bearish continuation is not confirmed.

Bar2 rallies to a high of 112, above the long bar's 111 high, so the counter-rally escapes the long bar's range. A counter-rally that clears the long bar's high is not the contained pause the pattern needs.
Bar1 closes at 104 below its 107 open, making it bearish. The three middle bars must be a bullish counter-rally; a bearish middle bar breaks the up-drift the pattern requires.
close[0]=99.5 is below the long bar's low[4]=100, so the strict close<low breakdown clause fires true. Kept clearly below 100 to avoid float-equality ambiguity.
Only change from breakdown-inside: close[0]=100.5 is above low[4]=100, so close<low is false. The final bar is still bearish, isolating the breakdown clause.
Bar1 low=100.1 is within the long bar's low[4]=100, so low[1]>=low[4] holds and containment passes. Everything else at positive canonical values.
Only change from containment-inside: bar1 low=99.9 is beyond low[4]=100, so low[1]>=low[4] fails. Single isolated change identifies the containment clause.

Mat hold bull: a long white bar (bar4: 100->107, range 8.5), a gap up so the first small bar (bar3) opens entirely above the long bar's 108 high (low[3]=108.5), three small consolidation bodies (0.2,0.3,0.3, each well under half the 8.5 range), then bar0 closes at 110.5, above the long bar's 108 high.

The anchor bar4 closes at 100 below its 107 open, making it bearish. Mat hold bull requires a long WHITE anchor; a bearish anchor cannot start a bullish continuation. Gap and breakout clauses stay intact so only the anchor direction fails.

The first small bar (bar3) has low=106, so it overlaps the long bar rather than gapping above its 108 high. Mat hold requires the consolidation to hold above the long bar (a rising window); without the gap up it is an ordinary pullback.

Bar2 has a body of 5.0 (109->104), larger than half the long bar's 8.5 range. The three middle bars must be small consolidation candles; a full-size body is not consolidation and the pattern must reject it.
Bar1 body=4.0 is under the 0.5*Range(4)=4.25 body ceiling, so Body(1)<=0.5*Range(4) holds. Margin ~6% below the threshold keeps it clear of float equality.
Only change from body-inside: bar1 body=4.5 is over the 0.5*Range(4)=4.25 ceiling, so Body(1)<=0.5*Range(4) fails. Isolates the body-size clause.
Bar3 low=108.2 is above the long bar's high[4]=108, so the strict low[3]>high[4] gap clause fires true. Kept above 108 with clear margin.
Only change from gap-inside: bar3 low=107.8 is below high[4]=108, so low[3]>high[4] is false. Isolates the gap clause.

Mat hold bear mirror: a long black bar (bar4: 108->101, range 8.5), a gap down so the first small bar (bar3) sits entirely below the long bar's 100 low (high[3]=99.5), three small consolidation bodies (0.2 each, under half the 8.5 range), then bar0 closes at 96.5, below the long bar's 100 low.

The anchor bar4 closes at 108 above its 101 open, making it bullish. Mat hold bear requires a long BLACK anchor; a bullish anchor cannot start a bearish continuation. Gap and breakdown clauses stay intact so only the anchor direction fails.

The first small bar (bar3) has high=101, so it overlaps the long bar rather than gapping below its 100 low. Mat hold bear requires the consolidation to hold below the long bar (a falling window); without the gap down it is an ordinary bounce.
Bar2 has a body of 5.0 (99->104), larger than half the long bar's 8.5 range. The middle bars must be small consolidation candles; a full-size body is not consolidation and the pattern must reject it.
Bar1 body=4.0 is under the 0.5*Range(4)=4.25 body ceiling, so Body(1)<=0.5*Range(4) holds. Margin ~6% below the threshold.
Only change from body-inside: bar1 body=4.5 is over the 0.5*Range(4)=4.25 ceiling, so Body(1)<=0.5*Range(4) fails. Isolates the body-size clause.
Bar3 high=99.8 is below the long bar's low[4]=100, so the strict high[3]<low[4] gap clause fires true. Kept below 100 with clear margin.
Only change from gap-inside: bar3 high=100.2 is above low[4]=100, so high[3]<low[4] is false. Isolates the gap clause.
An inside bar's whole range sits within the prior bar's range. Bar0 (high 103, low 97) is fully inside bar1 (high 105, low 95): high[0]<=high[1] and low[0]>=low[1]. Textbook consolidation bar.
Bar0 high=106 exceeds bar1 high=105, so the current bar pokes above the prior range. A bar that makes a higher high is not contained and is not an inside bar.
Bar0 low=94 undercuts bar1 low=95, so the current bar pokes below the prior range. A bar that makes a lower low is not contained and is not an inside bar.
Bar0 high=104.9 stays within bar1 high=105 and bar0 low=95.1 stays within bar1 low=95, so both containment inequalities hold. Just inside both bounds.
Bar0 high=105.1 is beyond bar1 high=105, so high[0]<=high[1] fails while the low stays contained. Isolates the high containment clause.
Bar0 low=94.9 is below bar1 low=95, so low[0]>=low[1] fails while the high stays contained. Isolates the low containment clause.
Two successive inside bars: bar1 (high 107, low 93) is inside bar2 (high 110, low 90), and bar0 (high 104, low 96) is inside bar1. A tightening two-step consolidation.
Bar0 high=108 exceeds bar1 high=107, so the newest bar is not inside its predecessor. The second inside relationship is broken, so it is not a double inside bar.
Bar1 low=89 undercuts bar2 low=90, so the middle bar is not inside the oldest bar. The first inside relationship is broken.
Bar1 high=111 exceeds bar2 high=110, so the middle bar breaks above the oldest bar. Attacks the outer high containment clause specifically.
Bar1 high=109.9 is within bar2 high=110, so high[1]<=high[2] holds; bar0 still inside bar1. Just inside the outer bound.
Only change from outer-inside: bar1 high=110.1 is beyond bar2 high=110, so high[1]<=high[2] fails. Isolates the outer high clause.
Bar0 low=93.1 is within bar1 low=93, so low[0]>=low[1] holds; the outer relationship stays intact. Just inside the inner bound.
Only change from inner-inside: bar0 low=92.9 is below bar1 low=93, so low[0]>=low[1] fails. Isolates the inner low clause.
An outside bar engulfs the prior bar's range. Bar0 (high 105, low 95) covers bar1 (high 103, low 97): high[0]>=high[1] and low[0]<=low[1]. A higher high and a lower low than the prior bar.
Bar0 high=102 fails to reach bar1 high=103, so the current bar does not engulf the top of the prior range. Without a higher high it is not an outside bar.
Bar0 low=98 fails to reach bar1 low=97, so the current bar does not engulf the bottom of the prior range. Without a lower low it is not an outside bar.
Bar0 (high 102, low 98) is fully inside bar1 (high 103, low 97): it is an inside bar, the exact opposite of engulfing. Both engulfing clauses fail.
Bar0 high=103.1 is above bar1 high=103 and bar0 low=96.9 is below bar1 low=97, so both engulfing inequalities hold. Just beyond both bounds on the engulfing side.
Bar0 high=102.9 is below bar1 high=103, so high[0]>=high[1] fails while the low still engulfs. Isolates the high engulfing clause (falls short of the top).
Bar0 low=97.1 is above bar1 low=97, so low[0]<=low[1] fails while the high still engulfs. Isolates the low engulfing clause (falls short of the bottom).
NR4 means the reference bar has the narrowest range of the last four bars. Bar0 range=1.0 is strictly smaller than bar1=2.0, bar2=3.0 and bar3=2.5. The narrowest bar of the group.
Bar1 range=0.8 is narrower than bar0 range=1.0, so bar0 is not the narrowest of the four. An NR4 requires the reference bar to be the single narrowest.

Bar0 range=1.0 exactly ties bar3 range=1.0. A tie means bar0 is not strictly the narrowest, so the pattern (narrowest of four) is not satisfied; the strict '<' comparison correctly rejects the tie. This is the tie-handling proof.
Bar0 range=10.0 is by far the widest of the four bars, the opposite of a narrow-range bar. Every range comparison fails.
Bar0 range=1.9 is below the smallest prior range (bar1=2.0, with bar2=3.0, bar3=2.5), so r0<Range(i) for all i and NR4 fires. Just under the nearest competitor.
Only change from NR4 boundary-inside: bar0 range=2.1 is above bar1 range=2.0, so r0<Range(1) fails. Just over the nearest competitor.
NR7 means the reference bar has the narrowest range of the last seven bars. Bar0 range=1.0 is strictly below all six older ranges (2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 2.4, 3.6). The narrowest of seven.
Bar5 range=0.9 is narrower than bar0 range=1.0, so bar0 is not the narrowest of the seven bars. NR7 requires the reference bar to be the single narrowest.
Bar0 range=1.0 exactly ties bar3 range=1.0, so bar0 is not strictly the narrowest of seven; the strict '<' comparison correctly rejects the tie. Tie-handling proof for the seven-bar window.
Bar0 range=12.0 is the widest bar of the seven, the opposite of a narrow-range bar. Fails against the very first comparison.
Bar0 range=1.9 is below the smallest prior range (bar1=2.0), so r0<Range(i) holds for all six older bars and NR7 fires. Just under the nearest competitor.
Only change from NR7 boundary-inside: bar0 range=2.1 is above bar1 range=2.0, so the loop finds r0>=Range(1) and returns false. Just over the nearest competitor.

A wide range bar's range dwarfs the recent average. The prior five bars each span 2.0 (ATR=2.0); bar0 spans 4.0, which is 2x the ATR and above the 1.5x expansion the pattern calls for. A clear volatility burst.
Bar0 spans 2.0, the same as the recent bars (ATR=2.0), so there is no expansion at all. A bar merely matching the average range is not a wide range bar.

Wide range is relative, not absolute. Here the recent bars each span 4.0 (ATR=4.0) and bar0 spans 5.0; 5.0 is only 1.25x the ATR, below the expansion threshold. A big bar in an already-volatile regime is not a wide range bar.

The prior five bars have zero range (flat, ATR=0), so there is no established volatility baseline for bar0 to be 'wide' relative to. With an undefined/zero reference the ratio cannot be formed and the bar is not classified as an expansion. See suspected_defect: pattern-wise a large bar after a dead-flat run is arguably the widest possible, but the atr>0 guard fails it closed.
ATR of the prior five bars is 2.0, so the 1.5x threshold is 3.0. Bar0 range=3.3 is above 3.0 (about 10% over), so r0>1.5*atr5 fires true.
Same ATR=2.0 baseline (threshold 3.0). Bar0 range=2.7 is below 3.0 (about 10% under), so r0>1.5*atr5 is false. Brackets the boundary from below.
